A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RepIt work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and matchable, including the retained, deliberately redacted example responses.

before.justification: V4 reports original jailbreak evaluations across five models, alongside localization, data-efficiency, projection, and category-generalization analyses.

after.justification: V5 retains those original results and adds Euclidean-orthogonalization ablations, principal-component analysis, and toxicity-targeting experiments.

M1.justification: The stated ACE intervention location changes from layer output in v4 Section 4.3 to layer input in v5 Section 4.2. The main reweighting, whitening, orthogonalization, and COSMIC procedures remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether this reported correction involved rerunning experiments.

E1.justification: V5 Appendix C.2 adds ToxiGen prompts targeting hateful demographic statements. This extends the targeted-jailbreak task beyond v4's biological, chemical, and cyber WMD concepts; previously, hate-related categories appeared among non-target concepts whose refusal should be preserved. Existing dataset coverage remains.

E2.justification: Appendix C.1 adds Euclidean partial orthogonalization without whitening or reweighting as an evaluated comparison to full RepIt. The existing unmodified-model, raw-DIM, and component comparisons remain. The toxicity experiment uses the existing comparator types.

E3.justification: The new Euclidean ablation introduces a control evaluated with its own selected rho values, as described in Appendix C.1. The retained experiments keep their splits, five models, generation caps, and LlamaGuard-3 scoring; v4 Appendix B.4 already disclosed that judge.

E4.justification: V5 adds a direct test of whether whitening and reweighting are necessary, plus PCA of the non-target basis to investigate the simplified procedure's behavior (Appendix C.1, Figures 8–9). These substantially extend the existing component, sparsity, data-efficiency, and projection analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report five seeds, 20–24, and means and ranges for the data-efficiency experiment in Figure 4. V5 introduces no additional repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their numerical entries. V5 adds substantial result sets: Euclidean-ablation ASRs, PCA curves showing over 90% variance within approximately ten components, and toxicity-target ASRs of approximately 0.46–0.88 across five models (Figures 8–10). These are newly reported outcomes, not improvements to retained same-setting results.

T1.justification: The core mathematical definitions, equations (1)–(8), and ACE rule are retained. Appendix C.1 specializes the existing projection operation for an ablation and offers informal conditioning explanations, without adding a substantive formal derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract refines localization from 100–200 neurons to 100–200 residual dimensions, although the introduction retains the earlier terminology. The principal claims about selective refusal suppression, evaluation evasion, and minimal data requirements remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 9 specifies white-box access and training, distribution, and serving adversaries. Appendix C.1 reframes whitening and reweighting as conservative safeguards despite the simplified ablation's effectiveness. V5 also adds interpretations involving low-rank structure, model size, and toxicity-specific geometry. The existing Appendix A limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: V5 specifies the numerical stabilizer as epsilon = 10^-6, explicitly locates activation extraction at layer inputs, and refines the hardware description in Appendix B.5. The code destination and statement that WMD prompts await controlled release remain unchanged. ToxiGen sample counts and splits are not supplied.

R1.justification: V5 adds citations for LlamaGuard's supporting model report, ToxiGen, and agent cooperation/security work. These support limited additions to evaluation and risk discussion; the existing related-work section and central novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: DIM background moves from Methodology Section 4.1 to Problem Setting Section 2.1. Sections 4, 6, and 7 receive local explanatory rewrites and subheadings, alongside the inserted threat model and new appendix. Most existing prose and the overall narrative sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: V5 adds Figures 8–10 and redraws Figures 1 and 3. Figure 3 places the final RepIt series, already reported in Figure 2, beside its component vectors and updates colors and legends. Figures 4 and 6 also move relative to surrounding text. Existing table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V5 improves assessability by extending v4's WMD-focused evidence, directly testing two method components, and specifying attacker-access assumptions. The gain is limited by missing ToxiGen sampling details and an inaccurate ablation summary: Appendix C.1 describes 1–3-point differences, while Figures 1 and 8 show approximately 0.43 versus 0.69 ASR for full RepIt and the retuned ablation on Phi4-mini/Bio. The added evidence is useful, but its interpretation needs correction.
